## 固定收益市場主線

9月29日，美債各期限走勢明顯分歧。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams表示不急於再度升息，帶動短天期殖利率下滑；30年期殖利率盤中卻突破5.61%，創2002年以來新高。職缺與消費者信心轉弱，進一步支撐短債，但這些數據加上油價回落，仍未能止住長債跌勢。市場依然面對大量公司債供給與不斷攀升的實質借款成本。

市場區分的是貨幣緊縮的時點，以及長期資金的價格。Williams並未放棄進一步緊縮，而是認為若經濟情勢符合預期，今年稍晚可能再升息一次。Paramount啟動收購融資中的優先債券發售後，因各部分需求不一，將更多借款轉向貸款。美國高收益債利差明顯擴大。海外市場方面，澳洲如預期升息，但總裁Michele Bullock對是否還需再次升息提出保留，反而帶動債市上漲；各國政府也因應異常昂貴的融資成本，調整發債安排。

## Williams放緩升息步調，美債曲線轉陡

美國政策訊息最明確的變化來自Williams。週二在水牛城大學演說時，他表示若經濟大致按預期發展，今年稍晚可能適合再次調升利率；9月升息已爭取到蒐集資訊的時間，因此沒有立即再動的迫切性。聯邦資金利率期貨隨即將10月27日至28日會議升息機率由70%降至約50%。Evercore ISI解讀，這番談話傾向10月暫停、12月再升息。

Williams身為FOMC永久投票委員及副主席，發言格外具有分量。他判斷是否進一步緊縮的條件，是基礎通膨趨勢與供需平衡，而非期中選舉將近；他明言選舉與決策無關。他目前預期能源影響將略為加大、持續更久，AI投資帶來的需求也愈來愈重要。不過，他尚未看到更廣泛且持久的外溢效應，並表示關稅已不再推升商品通膨。他預測今年通膨為3.5%，2027年略高於2%，2028年回到目標。

其他官員仍較強調進一步抑制需求的必要。聖路易聯準銀行總裁Alberto Musalem在倫敦表示，即使9月升息後，政策仍略偏寬鬆。芝加哥聯準銀行總裁Austan Goolsbee認為，若供給衝擊反覆發生或持續存在，聯準會可能必須回應，以維護2%目標的可信度，不能沿用通常不理會暫時性供給干擾的做法。理事Michael Barr在底特律表示，企業投資與具韌性的消費將支持下半年成長加速，但他仍看不到通膨能及時回到2%的明確路徑。因此，Williams的發言對近期升息時間表的改變，遠比對政策大方向的改變清楚。

美債行情也呈現這種區別。彭博9月29日每日殖利率序列顯示，2年期殖利率下跌5.4個基點至4.878%，5年期下跌2.2個基點至5.049%；10年期則上升1.7個基點至5.254%，30年期上升3.7個基點至5.585%。2年與10年期利差擴大7.1個基點至37.6個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大9.1個基點至70.7個基點。30年期殖利率連續第六天上升，盤中一度超過5.61%。

10年期實質殖利率上升2.9個基點至2.923%，損益兩平通膨率卻下跌1.2個基點至2.331%。換言之，名目殖利率上升時，長期通膨補償反而下降。Williams將長天期殖利率走高歸因於強勁的經濟前景、AI相關投資需求及油價帶來的反應，而非中長期通膨預期惡化。SMBC策略師Monty Gandhi也認為，週二部分長債賣壓來自Paramount規模異常龐大的債券發售。CIBC的Michael Cloherty則表示，足以穩定長天期美債、著眼價值的大型買家仍未出現。

當日數據削弱了對需求全面樂觀的理由。8月JOLTS職缺降至707.9萬個，低於市場預估的723萬個，也低於7月修正後的733.5萬個，創五個月低點。自願離職人數由修正後的308.9萬降至306.6萬，裁員仍少。這顯示雇主對增聘人手更加謹慎，卻未出現相應的裁員潮。

9月美國經濟評議會消費者信心指數下滑6.7點至81.9，創2014年以來最低，低於預估的89.2及下修後的前值88.6。現況指數下跌近8點，降至2021年以來低點；未來六個月預期指數也降至一年多來最低。9月1日至23日的調查顯示，各所得、年齡及地區族群的信心均惡化。有意購買汽車、住宅及大型家電的比例下降，預期所得增加的人也減少。

家庭對未來一年通膨的預期同樣轉差，預期利率上升的比例升至四年多來最高。認為工作機會充裕與認為工作難找的受訪者比例差距，縮至五年半多來最小。Pantheon Macroeconomics經濟學家Samuel Tombs與Oliver Allen認為，能源價格侵蝕實質所得，意味進一步緊縮應保持審慎。他們擔心的是，在實際支出尚未明顯全面下滑前，購買力已先遭到損害。

另有關於長期失業的報導，揭示低整體失業率之下的弱點。近200萬名美國人找工作已至少27週，近期平均求職時間也超過六個月。里奇蒙聯準銀行經濟學家Katarína Borovičková與Claudia Macaluso發現，通常擁有穩定、長年資工作的勞工，找到新工作的機率出現異常大幅惡化。受AI影響較深的職業降幅最大，但研究者表示，這項技術只能解釋長期失業上升的一小部分。過去一年，醫療與社會援助新增職位比其他所有類別加總還多。就業成長如此集中，對在其他產業求職的人而言，穩定的失業率就沒有那麼令人安心。

週二的區域與房市數據則好壞參半。9月達拉斯聯準銀行服務業指數由4.2降至負1.8，營收指數由6.6降至負0.9。相較之下，7月房價月增0.3%，高於預估的0.1%；年增率由前值2.3%升至2.6%。S&P/Case-Shiller房價年增率加快至2.5%，高於預估及修正後前值的2.2%，但月增率在前月上升0.4%後持平。截至9月26日當週，Redbook同店銷售年增率由7.6%升至8.2%。信心與招募轉弱的同時，部分名目支出及資產價格仍持續上升。

油價回落幅度明顯，長天期殖利率卻未跟進。11月WTI期貨收在$89.38，下跌3.48%，布蘭特原油收在$103以下。美國追加釋放戰略儲油，沙烏地阿拉伯東西向輸油管線恢復後也持續繞過荷莫茲海峽運油，共同緩解供應壓力，但外交僵局仍在。美元指數上漲0.19%至101.389；標普500指數下跌0.17%，那斯達克100指數上漲0.21%，半導體股上漲1.32%。股市反應仍有分歧，並非全面放棄科技成長題材。

最新部位分析顯示，數據一旦轉向，債市反應可能相當急促。5年期美債期貨未平倉量在十二個交易日中有十一日增加，10年期則在十四日中有十三日增加。自前一週開始，兩者合計增加的風險曝險約為每基點$3,200萬，相當於$750億的當期5年期現券。截至9月22日當週，資產管理公司增加超過10萬口10年期美債期貨空單總部位，不過避險及現券與期貨基差交易也可能促成這些操作。摩根大通另一份截至9月28日的客戶調查仍顯示，單邊多頭部位處於11月以來最高。期貨部位累積提高了弱數據引發快速平倉的可能，卻不能據此認定投資人一致看空。

## Paramount調整融資組合，利息負擔上升

Paramount Skydance週二正式推出第一順位擔保美元債，最初計畫透過八個期限、介於2年至40年的券種籌措約$320億。2066年到期券的初步討論為較美債加碼約365個基點。交易由Apollo、美國銀行及花旗主辦，公司預期週三定價；對高評級債而言，這樣的行銷時間異常長。

需求較偏向貸款，隨後促使融資結構調整。美元貸款由$65億增至$85億，歐元貸款則維持約$10億等值。較高評級債券在吸引超過$1,090億訂單後，計畫發行額減少$20億至約$300億。調整後，整體收購融資仍約$520億，其中包括約$124億等值的非投資等級債券。

週二下午稍早，兩筆貸款已吸引約$115億需求，美元部分超過$100億。更新後的貸款利差討論為基準利率加275個基點，初步區間上端原為300個基點。美元貸款發行價可能達面額的99.75%，歐元部分可能達面額，優於最初討論的99.5%折價發行。即使基準借款成本仍高，利差與發行價的改善，已降低貸款投資人要求的讓利。

非投資等級債券訂單則往反方向走。隨著定價討論推進，週二下午稍早訂單約$156億，低於週一超過$230億的初步意向。10年期美元債的殖利率仍在接近9%的水準討論，同評級流通債券約為7%。貸款需求增加、投機等級債券訂單縮小的反差，顯示投資人是依各部分的具體條件作出選擇，並非看到整體訂單龐大，就接受交易的所有部分。

新的發行文件更明確列出獲利假設。Paramount承諾在三年內達成每年$60億成本節省，使年化EBITDA由$127億增至$187億；按此假設，槓桿倍數約為4.4倍。部分節省將來自整合技術及企業軟體，以及縮減不動產。同時，公司仍須因應觀眾收視習慣改變，並履行每年推出30部院線電影的承諾。

CreditSights分析師Hunter Martin與Brian McKenna仍懷疑，Paramount能否單靠本業達成之後的槓桿目標，並認為節省成本的時程極為積極。評等機構按自身假設估計，收購完成後槓桿約為7倍，遠高於公司納入成本節省後的呈現。不過，CreditSights也認為Ellison家族的資源及投入，是重要的下檔支撐。彭博產業研究則提出營運面的正面對照：先前與Skydance整合的年度效率提升目標，已由約$20億提高至超過$30億。這項紀錄為整合能力提供一些信心，但不能將前一次整合與規模大得多的Warner交易等量齊觀。

融資負擔上升，使成本節省能否落實更為重要。CreditSights預估收購後總債務將超過$870億。知悉發售情況的人士估計，相較於年中前後發債，如今發行可能使借款成本增加約0.5至1個百分點，每年利息最多可能多出$5億。彭博產業研究的Stephen Flynn另以債券融資成本增加100至150個基點作假設估算，每年額外利息約為$4.5億至超過$6億。這些估計均取決於最終發行條件，但現金流影響很直接：利息增加，可用於還債的獲利就減少，公司將更依賴成本節省或資產出售。

## 澳洲升息，歐洲能源壓力暫獲緩解

澳洲如預期升息25個基點，將現金利率由4.35%調高至4.6%，創約十五年新高，九名理事一致同意。前兩次會議暫停後，這是2026年第四次升息，累計緊縮1個百分點。聲明強調國內需求具韌性，燃料成本已傳導至其他商品與服務；企業反映價格壓力，部分已漲價，部分正在考慮。

Bullock隨後的記者會改變了市場反應。她表示理事會曾考慮繼續暫停，也希望既有緊縮已足夠，但不願提供前瞻指引。3年期殖利率下跌8個基點，澳幣跌破0.70美元。貨幣市場將11月升息機率由發言前約61%降至約45%，預期現金利率高峰也降至5%以下。

澳洲國民銀行的Sally Auld認為，央行採取漸進方式，力求在降低通膨的同時保住勞動市場成果。限制正日益明顯：上月失業率升至4.6%，房市也已轉弱。然而，聲明仍明確表示，若有必要防止通膨根深蒂固，願意繼續升息。債市上漲反映對下一步的判斷轉柔，並不代表週二緊縮被推翻，也不是宣告升息循環結束。

西班牙則帶來新的通膨上行意外。9月消費者物價年增率由4.6%加快至5%，高於預估中位數4.9%，創2023年2月以來最高。燃料與套裝旅遊推升物價，基礎通膨指標漲幅也超過預期。西班牙國內經濟活動及觀光相對強勁，能源衝擊疊加在既有內生物價壓力之上，與預計通膨低於4%的其他歐元區成員形成更鮮明對比。

儘管如此，歐洲債券週二仍隨油價與天然氣價格下跌而上漲。報導稱歐盟官員不預期美國禁止柴油出口，加上卡達與華府、德黑蘭會談，緩解了能源焦慮。盤中報導顯示，英國10年期殖利率下跌近7個基點，2年及5年期均下跌6個基點，分別至4.87%及4.94%；德國10年期殖利率下跌5個基點至3.59%。交易員將截至2027年12月的預期累計緊縮幅度，下調至歐洲央行92個基點、英格蘭銀行110個基點。

英國標售仍鎖定了昂貴的融資成本。債務管理局出售£42.5億、票息4.875%、2036年7月到期的公債，平均得標殖利率5.383%，高於前次的5.16%，為1999年以來最高的10年期標售殖利率。投標倍數由逾3.6倍降至3.34倍。瑞穗的Evelyne Gomez-Liechti形容標售相對疲弱，即使殖利率較高，投資人仍不願拉長存續期間。

英國國內信用數據顯示，較高利率對不同借款人的影響不一。8月房貸核准件數連續第二個月下降，由下修後的55,928件降至54,918件，原先預期為持平，創2023年12月以來最低。消費借款卻達到創紀錄的£25億，高於六個月平均的£19億；信用卡淨借款由£9億增至£12億。KPMG的Katie Clinton表示，信心增強支持了借款，但也有家庭靠信用支付開銷。

首相Andy Burnham為財政辯論加入新的政治選項。他提出下次選舉後重新加入歐盟的可能性，承諾在今年稍晚的峰會提出方案；也承諾取消水公司公有化禁令，擴大政府對水務、能源及住宅的掌控。在房貸及政府借款成本已壓縮政策空間之際，這些提案的融資安排仍待決定。

加拿大面臨相關但不同的兩難。副總裁Toni Gravelle週二表示，高能源價格恐擴散至其他商品與服務，但美國貿易限制帶來的不確定性又可能削弱成長。美國對部分加拿大機車、酒精飲料及乳清產品的禁令當天上午生效。隔夜交換市場認為加拿大央行10月28日升息機率約五成，並反映截至6月升息100個基點，顯示通膨衝擊與貿易拖累之間的取捨仍未解。

## 各國調整新債規模與期限

紐西蘭提供了實際減少供給的例子。選前財政更新將截至2027年6月年度的預估營運赤字，由5月的NZ$114億下修至NZ$68億。債務高峰預測由GDP的46.1%降至2028年的43.9%，使紐西蘭債務管理局得以將未來四年的計畫發債量減少NZ$150億。公告後，10年期殖利率回吐稍早最多3個基點的升幅，在5.12%附近大致持平。

財政改善來自收入基礎轉強，而非迅速恢復盈餘。截至2026年6月的年度平均成長率為1.7%，高於5月預測的1.2%；財政部預期截至2027年6月將達2.3%，但營運收支仍要到2029年才會轉正。2030年淨核心政府債務預估為NZ$2,330億，低於先前的NZ$2,460億。財政部警告，油價已高於其假設，移民與生產力也可能不如預期。財政部長Nicola Willis明言，不會把改善後的數字視為可大開選舉支票的空間。

法國的供給方向正好相反。法國國庫署計畫2027年發行扣除買回後€3,400億的中長期債券，創歷史新高，較前一年增加約10%。國家總融資需求增加€280億至€3,397億，主因是需要再融資的到期債券增加€194億；其中很大部分來自疫情及2022年能源危機期間的借款。

官方數字顯示6月債務達GDP的119%，法債週二表現落後，10年期對德國公債利差約120個基點，為2012年以來最寬。法國國庫署署長Antoine Deruennes強調全球融資成本上升，以及各國政府與科技企業競逐資金，法國本身的預算又尚未定案。即使國會通過計畫中的€540億支出抑制措施，明年赤字也只會降至GDP的5%。因此，儘管提出財政節制，龐大的到期償付仍要求增加發債。

日本40年期公債標售顯示，較高長債殖利率與較小供給規模吸引買盤。投標倍數3.1倍，為2020年以來最強，高於前次2.82倍與十二個月平均2.67倍，5月調降標售規模也有幫助。SMBC日興證券的Rinto Maruyama另認為，市場預期更有力的政策緊縮，可能在推升短天期殖利率的同時，抑制長期通膨補償。三菱日聯資產管理的Masayuki Koguchi提醒，一次強勁標售尚不足以證明基本需求能持續。

菲律賓零售債計畫進入實際定價，週二在定價標售中籌得PHP849億。這批2.5年期、2029年到期債券票息為6.875%，相近期限既有債的BVAL殖利率為6.865%，吸引PHP1,886億投標。國庫署署長Sharon Almanza表示，政府目標為募集PHP1,500億新資金，另加換券，公開認購持續至10月7日。官員原曾考慮以25年期紀念零售債計畫週年，但最終選擇短年期，避免將高利率鎖定數十年。

泰國正為10月1日開始的會計年度考慮類似調整。債務管理部門主管Jindarat Viriyataveekul表示，新增融資與再融資初期可能採國庫券、定期貸款及本票，等條件改善後再轉為較長期證券。計畫新增借款為THB1.26兆。現有借款約89%屬長期，限制了存量債務立即重定價的幅度，目前平均成本接近2.6%。壓力更直接落在新發債上，而預估公共債務已接近GDP的69.7%，僅略低於70%上限。

中國的新刺激訊號可能增加地方政府發債，即使偏弱的信用需求仍支撐債市。前九個月只發行全年新增專項債額度的81%；按彭博計算，完成剩餘額度意味第四季發行超過人民幣8,200億元，為近五年最大單季規模。國務院也允許使用以前年度未動用額度，南華期貨的Gao Xiang估計可能再增加人民幣1,000億至2,000億元。

國務院承諾推出更多務實措施，擴大科技、農業與小企業再貸款，加快項目審批並提供貼息貸款。法國巴黎銀行的Jacqueline Rong認為，距離4.5%成長目標的差距不大，支持規模不必非常龐大；ING的Lynn Song則表示，更有力的房市措施對信心最重要。週二稍晚報導稱，北京已公布首購房貸利息補貼，並擴大基建與科技定向貸款。這些新措施，讓新增供給展望有了更直接對應的投資及家庭支持。

保加利亞透過三筆歐元債籌得€22.5億，需求超過€61億。2031年到期券增額發行€10億，定價為中間交換利率加60個基點；2034年到期券發行€7.5億，加95個基點；2044年到期券發行€5億，加160個基點，利差均較初步討論收窄。這是該國加入歐元區後第二次國際發債；雖然債務比率在歐盟名列最低之列，計畫赤字仍達GDP的5.7%。

墨西哥不斷擴大的國內退休基金，則提供另一種融資韌性。8月Afores持有墨西哥披索政府債券達創紀錄的MXN4.3兆，今年增加6%，較2025年初增加32%。其總資產預計由目前MXN9兆增至2030年的MXN12兆。惠譽的Todd Martinez表示，幾乎所有政府融資需求都能由國內滿足的能力，有助支撐主權評等。另外，墨西哥央行總裁Victoria Rodríguez反對機械式跟隨聯準會：經濟存在閒置產能，匯率傳遞效應又有限，容許央行獨立回應，但匯率影響與通膨預期仍是決策核心。她的論點說明，披索貶值並不必然迫使墨西哥升息。

## 市政債損失與AI集中風險影響投資人

市政債9月跌幅朝4.7%邁進，可能創1987年以來最差單月表現；截至週二紐約下午1時，指標殖利率最多上升3個基點。新數據顯示，週一成交117,419筆，至少為1995年以來最高。按面額計的成交金額$218億，高於近一年平均約$146億，但並非紀錄；異常龐大的是交易筆數，而非前所未見的成交金額。

9月供給已超過$510億，為2020年以來最高的同月規模。Clinton Investment Management的Andrew Clinton認為，買家被殖利率吸引、透過認列虧損節稅的交易、緊張情緒引發的賣出，以及為承接新券而調整投資組合，都促成交易活絡。富蘭克林坦伯頓的Ben Barber表示，儘管賣方向市場徵求買價的活動創紀錄，交易大致仍有秩序。10年期市政債殖利率約為相同期限美債的80%，30年期約95%，相對價值吸引力提高，卻仍無法阻止價格續跌。

Brightline帶來個別借款人的估值壓力。週二報導指出，Nuveen是週一以整包成交、不可拆售方式，按面額45%出售約$1.9億優先無保險債券的賣方。2053年到期券在9月17日仍交易於面額約64%。First Eagle持有約$2.26億，為這批優先無保險債券最大持有人，與其他剩餘投資人一同面臨潛在估值下修。其高收益市政債基金週一下跌2.7%，Nuveen旗艦高收益基金跌約2%。

Nuveen表示，自2023年4月以來已減少Brightline曝險逾75%，並透過重整保護剩餘的第三順位擔保及通勤鐵路相關配置。對已出售的優先債券，擬議方案是將截至2028年1月應支付的三次利息，遞延至2031年1月。另外，Brightline律師Paul Leake週二向破產法院表示，持有約$10億債權的兩組債權人已加入重整支持協議，使支持債務總額增至約$46億。退出破產程序方案獲得更廣泛支持的同時，次級市場價格卻大幅降低；兩者分別影響法律程序進度與基金估值。

結構型信用方面，PGIM披露一種跨越傳統產業分類的AI曝險限制方式。它作為主要投資人參與上週發行、由法國巴黎銀行安排的$5億Allstate CLO，並設置15%的AI相關擔保資產上限。PGIM逐筆評分貸款與AI產業的關聯程度，包括為規劃中資料中心供電的公用事業等間接曝險。一旦加總分數超過15%，這檔CLO便不得再增加AI相關債務。其他採類似限制的交易正在討論，尚未定案。

PGIM的Edwin Wilches估計，目前$1.4兆CLO市場中的AI債務僅占2%至3%，但隨融資擴張，分散風險將愈來愈困難。美國銀行策略師估計，晶片與資料中心定期貸款曝險可能由約$45億增至$1,000億。這項契約創新針對的是名義上不同產業之間相互關聯的現金流，而非單純設定傳統的科技業上限。

新研究也質疑，這波投資能否創造足夠收入來支撐融資。貝恩年度科技報告估計，到2031年，AI每年需要$6兆收入，才能支持已投入的資料中心資本，但現有消費者與企業服務可能只能產生$1.8兆。主要作者David Crawford表示，要讓融資可持續，全球GDP每年成長率須額外增加約1個百分點。渣打經濟學家Dan Pan與Steve Englander指出另一項主權財政限制：1990年代末，企業稅收增加額相當於GDP的0.5%，使企業稅收占GDP比率升至2.1%，但目前企業稅收占比更低，難以重演當年情況。所得稅與薪資稅占收入80%，即使科技投資成功，人口老化與移民減少仍可能限制財政受益。

美國固定收益市場收盤後，彭博Odd Lots電子報提出新的短期融資疑慮。3個月國庫券殖利率高於SOFR OIS 9個基點，6個月則高出13個基點。巴克萊的Samuel Earl形容，這是今年最高的相對水準，與2025年第四季貨幣市場波動期間相當。若國庫券持續相對走弱，壓力可能傳至附買回市場，最終影響有效聯邦資金利率。評論提到聯準會上月暫停準備金管理購債後，可能恢復此類購買，但並未報導新的干預行動。

## 後續市場觀察

9月30日將同時迎來通膨與就業數據，直接檢驗Williams主張等待的空間。ADP將於紐約時間上午8時15分公布，9月民間就業預估增加7萬人，前值為3.8萬人。上午8時30分公布的8月核心PCE物價，預估月增0.3%，高於前月0.2%，年增3.3%；整體PCE物價預估月增0.4%。支出預估增加0.8%，所得增加0.4%。支出數字有助判斷信心疲弱是否開始抑制購買，通膨則直接影響聯準會9月升息後能等待多久。

10月1日將公布失業救濟申請與ISM製造業指數，後者預估由54.6升至55，價格指數由71.1升至72.3。10月2日非農就業預估增加9萬人，低於前月16.2萬人；失業率預估維持4.1%，薪資月增0.3%。若招募放慢但失業未增加，將延續週二所見的低招募景象；若惡化超過這個程度，對日益增加的美債期貨空單可能帶來格外大的衝擊。Barkin、Goolsbee、Kashkari與Williams後續發言，將顯示聯準會內部是否有更多人區分最終仍需緊縮與立即採取行動。

澳洲週三公布月度通膨，緊接在本次升息之後；相較於聲明最初傳達的訊息，市場對後續升息的預期較為保留。歐元區週五通膨預估為3.7%，將在西班牙數據高於預期、歐洲能源價格回落之後公布。日本週三2年期標售，則在40年期需求強勁後，檢驗對政策敏感的短債需求。三者各有不同考驗：近期通膨是否持續、歐洲物價加速的涵蓋範圍，以及投資人持有短天期日債的意願。

Paramount預計週三定價，必須將調整後的訂單轉化為最終融資成本。轉向貸款已改善該部分條件，但非投資等級債券需求縮小，使發行讓利仍攸關公司的降槓桿計畫。法國週四提出預算，必須釐清在計畫發債規模創紀錄之際，支出抑制措施能否取得國會支持。能源方面，美國追加釋放儲油帶來實際供給紓解，但荷莫茲海峽談判未解，高燃料成本能持續多久，仍是家庭需求與貨幣政策的核心變數。

另看週三台北時間上午7時15分前的亞洲早盤，美債前一交易日漲跌互見後，紐西蘭債券上漲；WTI約跌0.8%至$88.70。亞洲開盤延續能源價格回落，但已結束的美國交易日留下的是更陡的殖利率曲線，以及仍在上升的長期借款成本。

overall_summary.headline: Williams釋出耐心訊號，美債曲線轉陡，長期借款成本仍攀升
overall_summary.session_narrative:
John Williams表示，9月升息已讓聯準會有時間蒐集資訊，今年稍晚可能適合再動，卻無須急於升息。10月升息機率由70%降至約50%。職缺減少至707.9萬個，消費者信心降至81.9，進一步支撐短天期美債，卻未能終止長債賣壓。

2年期殖利率下跌5.4個基點至4.878%，30年期則上升3.7個基點至5.585%，盤中曾超過5.61%，創2002年以來新高。10年期實質殖利率上升，通膨補償卻下降，說明長期資金所承受的壓力不只是通膨預期升高。Paramount大規模收購融資啟動，增添供給壓力，美國高收益債利差也明顯擴大。

Paramount將原訂較高評級債券中的$20億轉入美元貸款；貸款條件改善，非投資等級債券訂單卻減少。最終利息負擔仍攸關還債能力。海外方面，澳洲將現金利率升至4.6%，但Michele Bullock對再次升息的必要性提出保留後，債券反而上漲。9月30日的就業與通膨數據將檢驗聯準會還有多少等待空間。
overall_summary.summary: 招募與信心轉弱支撐短天期美債，但實質殖利率上升與大量公司債供給，讓長債即使面對油價回落，仍承受壓力。

section_summaries.summary: 市場區分進一步緊縮的時點與長期資金成本。Williams降低了再度升息的迫切性，但美國數據轉弱、油價回落仍未能止住長債跌勢。Paramount因需求分歧調整融資，高收益債利差明顯擴大；澳洲債市上漲則源於下一次升息訊息轉柔，並非緊縮反轉。

section_summaries.section_title: Williams放緩升息步調，美債曲線轉陡
section_summaries.summary: Williams傾向多花時間評估9月升息，其他聯準會官員仍擔心通膨持續。職缺與信心轉弱支撐短債，2年與10年期利差擴大7.1個基點。即使油價與通膨補償下降，實質殖利率上升及公司債供給仍壓抑長債。期貨空單增加可能放大弱數據引發的平倉，但投資人部位並非一致看空。

section_summaries.section_title: Paramount調整融資組合，利息負擔上升
section_summaries.summary: Paramount在約$520億融資方案中，將美元貸款增至$85億，較高評級債券計畫額降至約$300億。貸款利差改善，非投資等級債券訂單卻縮小，10年期美元債殖利率仍接近9%。公司$60億成本節省計畫推算的槓桿為4.4倍，評等機構估計交易完成後卻約為7倍。利息成本升高，減少可用於還債的現金，也提高對落實成本節省或出售資產的依賴。

section_summaries.section_title: 澳洲升息，歐洲能源壓力暫獲緩解
section_summaries.summary: 澳洲升息至4.6%，但Bullock表達希望既有緊縮已足夠後，3年期殖利率下跌8個基點。西班牙通膨加速至5%，歐洲債券仍受能源降價帶動上漲。英國房貸核准件數下滑、消費信用增加之際，10年期標售殖利率仍創1999年以來新高。加拿大則同時面對能源通膨壓力與美國新貿易限制。

section_summaries.section_title: 各國調整新債規模與期限

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries split sharply by maturity on September 29: shorter yields fell as New York Fed President John Williams pushed back against an urgent follow-up rate increase, while the 30-year yield crossed 5.61% during trading, its highest since 2002. Weak job openings and consumer confidence gave the front end additional support, but neither those releases nor cheaper oil stopped the long-bond decline. Investors still faced substantial corporate supply and rising real borrowing costs.

The distinction was between the timing of monetary tightening and the price of long-term capital. Williams envisaged one more increase late this year, conditional on the economy, rather than abandoning further restraint. Paramount launched the senior-bond portion of its acquisition financing and subsequently shifted more borrowing into loans as demand diverged across the package. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably. Overseas, Australia's expected rate increase produced a bond rally after Governor Michele Bullock questioned the need for another move, while sovereign borrowers changed issuance plans to accommodate unusually expensive funding.

## Williams Slows the Clock as the Treasury Curve Steepens

Williams supplied the clearest change in the U.S. policy message. Speaking at the University at Buffalo on Tuesday, the New York Fed president said another upward adjustment might be appropriate late this year if the economy developed broadly as he expected. September's increase had bought time to gather information, he said, leaving no urgency to move again. Federal funds futures immediately reduced the probability of an October 27-28 increase to about 50% from 70%. Evercore ISI interpreted the remarks as favoring an October pause followed by a December increase.

As a permanent FOMC voter and its vice chair, Williams carries particular weight. His condition for further tightening concerned underlying inflation trends and the balance of supply and demand, not the proximity of the midterm elections, which he said was irrelevant to the decision. He now expected somewhat larger and more persistent energy effects, alongside increasingly important demand from AI investment. Nevertheless, he saw no evidence yet of broader, persistent spillovers and said tariffs were no longer adding to goods inflation. His forecast put inflation at 3.5% this year, just above 2% in 2027 and at target in 2028.

Other officials maintained a stronger emphasis on additional restraint. In London, St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem said policy remained somewhat accommodative even after September's increase. Chicago's Austan Goolsbee argued that repeated or lasting supply shocks could require a response to preserve the credibility of the 2% target, departing from the usual practice of looking through temporary supply disturbances. Governor Michael Barr, speaking in Detroit, expected growth to accelerate in the second half, supported by business investment and resilient consumption, and still saw no clear path back to 2% inflation in a timely manner. Williams' intervention therefore changed the near-term timetable more clearly than the prevailing direction of policy.

The Treasury market reflected that distinction. Bloomberg's September 29 daily yield series put the two-year at 4.878%, down 5.4 basis points, and the five-year at 5.049%, down 2.2. The 10-year rose 1.7 basis points to 5.254%, while the 30-year increased 3.7 to 5.585%. The 2s10s curve steepened 7.1 basis points to 37.6, and 2s30s widened 9.1 to 70.7. During the session, the long bond's yield exceeded 5.61% as it rose for a sixth consecutive day.

At 10 years, real yields climbed 2.9 basis points to 2.923%, while the breakeven declined 1.2 to 2.331%. The nominal increase consequently came with lower, not higher, long-term inflation compensation. Williams attributed higher long yields to the strong economic outlook, AI-related investment demand and the response to oil prices, rather than a deterioration in medium- or long-term inflation expectations. SMBC strategist Monty Gandhi also connected part of Tuesday's long-end selling to Paramount's unusually large bond launch. CIBC's Michael Cloherty said the substantial value buyer that might stabilize long Treasuries had still not appeared.

The day's economic releases weakened the case for indiscriminate optimism about demand. August JOLTS openings fell to 7.079 million, below the 7.23 million consensus and a revised 7.335 million in July. That was a five-month low. Quits declined to 3.066 million from a revised 3.089 million, while layoffs remained subdued. The combination pointed to employers becoming more cautious about hiring without a corresponding wave of dismissals.

September Conference Board confidence fell 6.7 points to 81.9, its lowest since 2014, against a consensus of 89.2 and a downwardly revised 88.6 previously. The present-conditions measure dropped nearly 8 points to its lowest since 2021, and expectations for the next six months reached a more than one-year low. Deterioration extended across income groups, ages and regions in the September 1-23 survey. Smaller shares intended to purchase vehicles, homes and major appliances, while fewer expected their incomes to grow.

Households also anticipated worse inflation over the next year, and the share expecting higher interest rates reached its highest in more than four years. The difference between respondents saying jobs were plentiful and those saying they were hard to find narrowed to its smallest in more than five and a half years. Pantheon Macroeconomics economists Samuel Tombs and Oliver Allen argued that energy's squeeze on real incomes warranted caution over further tightening. Their concern was the damage to purchasing power even before a broad decline in realized spending became apparent.

Separate reporting on prolonged unemployment exposed another weakness beneath the low headline jobless rate. Nearly 2 million Americans had been looking for work for at least 27 weeks, and the average search had recently exceeded six months. Richmond Fed economists Katarína Borovičková and Claudia Macaluso found an unusually large deterioration in job-finding rates among workers normally attached to stable, long-tenured jobs. The drop was greatest in occupations exposed to AI, although the researchers said the technology explained only a small part of rising long-term unemployment. Healthcare and social assistance had generated more jobs over the past year than all other categories combined. That narrow distribution makes a stable unemployment rate less reassuring for workers seeking employment elsewhere.

Tuesday's regional and housing figures were mixed. The Dallas Fed services index fell to minus 1.8 in September from 4.2, and its revenue measure declined to minus 0.9 from 6.6. July house prices, by contrast, increased 0.3% monthly against a 0.1% consensus, with annual growth of 2.6% versus 2.3% previously. The S&P/Case-Shiller annual measure accelerated to 2.5%, above the 2.2% consensus and revised prior reading, although its monthly measure was flat after a 0.4% increase. Redbook same-store sales growth reached 8.2% for the week ended September 26, from 7.6%. The weaker confidence and hiring observations thus coexisted with continuing increases in some nominal spending and asset prices.

Oil eased more decisively than long yields. November WTI settled at $89.38, down 3.48%, and Brent settled below $103. An additional U.S. emergency-reserve release helped relieve pressure while the restored Saudi East-West pipeline continued carrying oil around Hormuz. The diplomatic stalemate persisted. The Dollar Index gained 0.19% to 101.389; the S&P 500 fell 0.17%, while the Nasdaq 100 added 0.21% and semiconductor shares gained 1.32%. The equity response remained uneven rather than a wholesale abandonment of technology growth.

New positioning analysis showed how abruptly a change in the data could affect bonds. Five-year futures open interest had risen in eleven of twelve sessions and 10-year open interest in thirteen of fourteen. Since the start of the previous week, the combined added risk amounted to about $32 million per basis point, equivalent to $75 billion of the current five-year cash note. Asset managers added more than 100,000 gross 10-year futures shorts in the week ended September 22, although hedges and cash-futures basis trades can also contribute to that activity. JPMorgan's separate client survey through September 28 still showed outright longs at their highest since November. The futures buildup increases the potential for a rapid unwind on weak data without establishing a uniformly bearish investor base.

## Paramount Rebalances Its Financing as the Interest Bill Rises

Paramount Skydance formally launched its first-lien dollar bond offering Tuesday, initially seeking about $32 billion across eight maturities from two to 40 years. Initial discussion on the 2066 maturity was around 365 basis points over Treasuries. The company expected pricing Wednesday, an unusually extended marketing period for high-grade debt, with Apollo, Bank of America and Citigroup leading the transaction.

The financing structure then changed as demand favored loans. The dollar loan was increased to $8.5 billion from $6.5 billion, while the euro loan remained about $1 billion-equivalent. The planned higher-rated bond amount fell by $2 billion to approximately $30 billion after attracting more than $109 billion of orders. Those adjustments kept the wider acquisition package around $52 billion, including roughly $12.4 billion-equivalent of junk bonds.

Early Tuesday afternoon, the two loan tranches had attracted about $11.5 billion of demand, more than $10 billion of it for the dollar piece. Revised loan discussions put margins at 275 basis points over benchmark rates, against an initial range reaching 300. The dollar issue price could reach 99.75 cents and the euro tranche par, compared with an initial 99.5-cent discount. The improvement in margin and issue price reduced the concession demanded by lenders even as benchmark borrowing costs remained high.

The junk-bond book moved in the other direction. Orders stood around $15.6 billion early Tuesday afternoon, down from more than $23 billion of preliminary interest Monday as pricing discussions progressed. A 10-year dollar note was still being discussed near a 9% yield, against about 7% for similarly rated outstanding debt. The contrast between expanding loan demand and a smaller speculative-grade bond book showed investors responding to the specific offered terms rather than accepting every part of the transaction on the strength of its headline order total.

New offering documents made the earnings assumptions more explicit. Paramount promised $6 billion of annual cost savings within three years, lifting annualized EBITDA to $18.7 billion from $12.7 billion. On those assumptions, leverage would be about 4.4 times. The savings would come partly from combining technology and enterprise software and reducing real estate. The company simultaneously has to accommodate changing viewing habits and its commitment to release 30 films a year in cinemas.

CreditSights analysts Hunter Martin and Brian McKenna remained skeptical that Paramount could reach its later leverage goals organically, calling the savings timetable highly aggressive. The rating agencies' own assumptions put leverage around seven times after completion, substantially above the company's savings-adjusted presentation. CreditSights nevertheless identified the Ellison family's resources and commitment as important downside support. Bloomberg Intelligence offered an operating counterpoint: the targeted annual efficiencies from the earlier Skydance combination had increased from roughly $2 billion to more than $3 billion. That record supports some confidence in execution, without equating the earlier integration with the much larger Warner transaction.

The higher financing burden makes delivery more consequential. CreditSights expects total debt exceeding $87 billion after the acquisition. People familiar with the offering estimated that issuing now instead of around midyear could add roughly 0.5-1 percentage point to borrowing costs and potentially as much as $500 million in annual interest. Bloomberg Intelligence's Stephen Flynn described a separate hypothetical 100-150-basis-point increase on the bond financing, or about $450 million to more than $600 million a year. These are estimates dependent on the eventual sale terms, but the cash-flow consequence is straightforward: additional interest leaves less earnings available for debt repayment, increasing reliance on savings or asset sales.

## Australia Hikes While Europe Gets Partial Energy Relief

Australia delivered the anticipated quarter-point increase, taking the cash rate from 4.35% to 4.6%, its highest in about 15 years. The nine-member board was unanimous. Its fourth rise of 2026 brought cumulative tightening to a percentage point after pauses at the preceding two meetings. The statement emphasized resilient domestic demand and fuel costs already passing into other goods and services, with firms reporting price pressure and either raising prices or considering doing so.

Bullock's subsequent press conference altered the market response. She said the board had considered extending the pause and expressed hope that the tightening already delivered would prove sufficient, while declining to give forward guidance. Three-year yields fell 8 basis points and the Australian dollar dropped below 70 U.S. cents. Money markets cut the probability of a November increase to about 45% from about 61% before her remarks, and the expected peak cash rate moved below 5%.

National Australia Bank's Sally Auld saw an incremental approach designed to reduce inflation while preserving labor-market gains. The constraint is becoming more visible: unemployment reached 4.6% last month and housing is already weakening. Yet the statement retained an explicit willingness to raise rates further if needed to prevent inflation becoming embedded. The rally followed a softer assessment of the next step, not a reversal of Tuesday's tightening or a declaration that the cycle was over.

Spain supplied a fresh upside inflation surprise. September consumer-price growth accelerated to 5% from 4.6%, above the 4.9% median forecast and the highest since February 2023. Fuel and package holidays drove the increase, while the underlying measure also rose more than expected. Spain's relatively strong domestic activity and tourism leave it facing an energy shock on top of existing homegrown pressure. The result sharpened the distinction between that economy and euro-area members expected to report inflation below 4%.

European bonds nevertheless gained during Tuesday's trading as oil and gas fell. Reports that EU officials did not expect a U.S. diesel-export ban, alongside Qatari meetings with Washington and Tehran, helped reduce energy anxiety. UK 10-year yields were almost 7 basis points lower in the intraday account; two- and five-year gilt yields fell 6 basis points to 4.87% and 4.94%. Germany's 10-year yield declined 5 basis points to 3.59%. Traders reduced the tightening priced through December 2027 to 92 basis points for the ECB and 110 for the Bank of England.

Britain's auction still locked in expensive financing. The Debt Management Office sold £4.25 billion of 4.875% July 2036 bonds at an average yield of 5.383%, compared with 5.16% at the previous sale, the highest 10-year auction yield since 1999. Bid coverage fell to 3.34 times from more than 3.6. Mizuho's Evelyne Gomez-Liechti described the sale as relatively weak, with investors reluctant to extend duration despite higher yields.

The domestic credit figures showed that higher rates were affecting borrowers unevenly. August mortgage approvals fell for a second month to 54,918, from a downwardly revised 55,928, against expectations of no change. That was the lowest since December 2023. Consumer borrowing instead reached a record £2.5 billion, above its six-month average of £1.9 billion; net credit-card borrowing rose to £1.2 billion from £900 million. KPMG's Katie Clinton said greater confidence supported borrowing, but some households were also using credit to cover expenses.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham added new political choices to the fiscal debate, raising the possibility of rejoining the EU after the next election and promising options at a summit later this year. He also pledged to remove the ban on public ownership of water companies and expand public control over water, energy and housing. The proposals leave financing decisions ahead as expensive mortgages and government borrowing already constrain policy room.

Canada faced a related but distinct conflict. Deputy Governor Toni Gravelle said Tuesday that high energy prices threatened to spread into other goods and services while uncertainty from U.S. trade restrictions could weaken growth. A U.S. ban on selected Canadian motorcycles, alcoholic beverages and whey products took effect that morning. Overnight swaps assigned roughly even odds to an October 28 Bank of Canada increase and priced 100 basis points of tightening by June, reflecting the unresolved balance between the inflation shock and trade-related restraint.

## Sovereigns Change the Amount and Maturity of New Debt

New Zealand provided a concrete reduction in supply. Its pre-election fiscal update cut the projected operating deficit for the year through June 2027 to NZ$6.8 billion from NZ$11.4 billion in May. The debt peak is now forecast at 43.9% of GDP in 2028 rather than 46.1%, allowing New Zealand Debt Management to reduce planned bond sales by NZ$15 billion over four years. The 10-year yield erased an earlier increase of as much as 3 basis points and was little changed at 5.12% after the announcement.

The improvement reflects a stronger revenue base rather than a rapid return to surplus. Annual average growth through June 2026 was 1.7%, above the May projection of 1.2%, and Treasury expects 2.3% by June 2027. The operating balance is still not forecast to turn positive until 2029. Net core Crown debt is projected at NZ$233 billion by 2030, below the earlier NZ$246 billion estimate. Treasury warned that oil was already more expensive than its assumptions and that immigration and productivity could disappoint. Finance Minister Nicola Willis ruled out treating the better figures as room for generous election promises.

France announced the opposite supply direction. Agence France Trésor plans €340 billion of medium- and long-term issuance net of buybacks in 2027, a record and about 10% more than the preceding year. Total state financing needs rise €28 billion to €339.7 billion, chiefly because maturing bonds requiring replacement increase €19.4 billion. Much of that refinancing relates to borrowing undertaken during the pandemic and the 2022 energy crisis.

French bonds underperformed Tuesday as official figures put debt at 119% of GDP in June. The 10-year premium over Germany was around 120 basis points, its widest since 2012. AFT chief Antoine Deruennes emphasized the global rise in funding costs and competition from sovereign and technology borrowers, while the country's own budget remains unsettled. The planned €54 billion spending-containment effort would reduce next year's deficit only to 5% of GDP even if parliament adopts it. Large redemptions therefore require additional issuance despite the proposed fiscal restraint.

Japan's 40-year auction showed buyers responding to long yields and a smaller supply schedule. Bids covered the offering 3.1 times, the strongest ratio since 2020, against 2.82 at the preceding sale and a 12-month average of 2.67. May's reduction in auction sizes helped. SMBC Nikko's Rinto Maruyama also argued that expectations of more forceful policy tightening could restrain long-run inflation compensation even while pushing up shorter yields. Mitsubishi UFJ Asset Management's Masayuki Koguchi cautioned that one strong sale was insufficient to establish durable underlying demand.

The Philippines converted its planned retail sale into actual terms, raising PHP84.9 billion at Tuesday's price-setting auction. The 2.5-year 2029 bonds carry a 6.875% coupon, against a BVAL yield of 6.865% on existing debt of comparable maturity, and attracted PHP188.6 billion of bids. Treasurer Sharon Almanza said the government targets PHP150 billion of new money, plus exchanges, with public subscriptions continuing through October 7. Officials had considered a 25-year maturity to commemorate the retail program's anniversary but selected the short tenor to avoid locking in high rates for decades.

Thailand is considering a similar adjustment for its fiscal year beginning October 1. Debt-office head Jindarat Viriyataveekul said new funding and refinancing might initially use Treasury bills, term loans and promissory notes, with conversion to longer securities when conditions improve. Planned new borrowing is THB1.26 trillion. About 89% of existing borrowing is long-term, limiting the immediate repricing of the outstanding portfolio, whose average cost is near 2.6%. The pressure falls more directly on new issuance as projected public debt approaches 69.7% of GDP, just below the 70% ceiling.

China's new stimulus signals could increase local-government issuance even while weak credit demand supports bonds. Only 81% of the annual new special-bond quota had been sold through the first nine months. Completing it would imply more than CNY820 billion in Q4, the largest quarterly amount in almost five years, according to Bloomberg calculations. The State Council also allowed unused quotas from earlier years to be tapped; Nanhua Futures' Gao Xiang estimated that could add CNY100 billion-CNY200 billion.

The cabinet promised additional practical measures, expanded relending for technology, agriculture and small businesses, faster project approvals and discounted loans. BNP Paribas' Jacqueline Rong judged the gap to the 4.5% growth goal modest enough that support need not be enormous, while ING's Lynn Song said stronger housing measures would matter most for confidence. Later Tuesday reporting said Beijing had unveiled interest-payment subsidies for first-home mortgages and expanded targeted lending for infrastructure and technology. The fresh measures give the supply outlook a more immediate counterpart in prospective investment and household support.

Bulgaria meanwhile placed €2.25 billion across three euro tranches with demand exceeding €6.1 billion. The 2031 reopening raised €1 billion at 60 basis points over mid-swaps; €750 million due in 2034 priced at 95, and €500 million due in 2044 at 160. Spreads tightened from initial discussion. Its second international transaction since joining the euro area comes against a planned deficit of 5.7% of GDP, despite one of the EU's lowest debt ratios.

Mexico's expanding domestic pension base offered another source of funding resilience. Afores held a record MXN4.3 trillion in government peso debt in August, up 6% this year and 32% since the start of 2025. Their total assets are expected to reach MXN12 trillion by 2030 from MXN9 trillion now. Fitch's Todd Martinez said the capacity to meet almost all government funding domestically supports the sovereign rating. Separately, Banxico Governor Victoria Rodríguez rejected mechanically matching Fed moves: spare capacity and limited currency pass-through permit an independent response, although exchange-rate effects and inflation expectations remain central to decisions. Her argument qualified the assumption that peso depreciation must automatically force Mexican tightening.

## Municipal Losses and AI Concentration Reach Investors

Municipal bonds were heading for a 4.7% September loss, potentially the worst month since 1987, while benchmark yields rose as much as 3 basis points by 1 p.m. New York Tuesday. New data showed 117,419 trades Monday, the most since at least 1995. Par turnover of $21.8 billion was above the roughly $14.6 billion one-year average but not a record, distinguishing unusually heavy transaction counts from unprecedented dollar volume.

Supply had already exceeded $51 billion in September, the most for that month since 2020. Clinton Investment Management's Andrew Clinton attributed activity to buyers attracted by yields, tax-loss transactions, nervous selling and portfolio changes to accommodate new issues. Franklin Templeton's Ben Barber said trading remained broadly orderly despite record bid-wanted activity. Ten-year munis offered around 80% of comparable Treasury yields and 30-year debt around 95%, increasing relative-value appeal without preventing further price declines.

Brightline added a borrower-specific source of valuation pressure. Reporting Tuesday identified Nuveen as the seller of approximately $190 million of senior uninsured bonds in an all-or-nothing portfolio transaction Monday at 45 cents on the dollar. The 2053 bonds had traded near 64 cents on September 17. First Eagle, the largest holder of the senior uninsured debt at about $226 million, faced potential markdowns alongside other remaining investors. Its high-yield municipal fund fell 2.7% Monday, while Nuveen's flagship high-yield fund dropped about 2%.

Nuveen said it had cut Brightline exposure more than 75% since April 2023 and protected its remaining third-lien and commuter allocations through restructuring. The proposed treatment of the senior bonds sold involves deferring three interest payments due through January 2028 until January 2031. Separately, Brightline's lawyer Paul Leake told the bankruptcy court Tuesday that two creditor groups owed about $1 billion had joined the restructuring support agreement, bringing backing to roughly $4.6 billion of debt. Broader support for the exit proposal and a substantially lower secondary price thus developed together, with different implications for legal progress and fund valuations.

In structured credit, PGIM disclosed a new way of limiting AI exposure that cuts across conventional industry categories. It anchored a $500 million Allstate CLO issued last week and arranged by BNP Paribas with a 15% AI-related collateral limit. PGIM scores individual loans for their connection to the industry, including indirect exposures such as utilities serving prospective data centers. Once the aggregate score exceeds 15%, the vehicle cannot add more AI-linked debt. Other transactions with similar restrictions are being discussed but are not finalized.

PGIM's Edwin Wilches put current AI debt in the $1.4 trillion CLO market at only 2%-3%, but expected diversification to become harder as financing expands. Bank of America strategists estimate chip and data-center term-loan exposure could grow to $100 billion from about $4.5 billion. The contractual innovation responds to correlated cash flows across nominally separate sectors, rather than simply setting a conventional technology-sector cap.

Fresh research also questioned how the investment wave will finance itself. Bain's annual technology report estimated AI would need $6 trillion of annual revenue by 2031 to justify deployed data-center capital, with existing consumer and enterprise services potentially producing only $1.8 trillion. Lead author David Crawford said sustainable funding would require roughly a percentage point of additional annual global GDP growth. Standard Chartered economists Dan Pan and Steve Englander identified a separate sovereign limitation: corporate tax receipts increased 0.5% of GDP to 2.1% in the late 1990s, but today's lower corporate-tax take makes a repeat unlikely. With income and payroll taxes providing 80% of revenue, aging and reduced immigration could limit the fiscal dividend even if technology investment succeeds.

After the U.S. fixed-income close, Bloomberg's Odd Lots newsletter highlighted a new short-term funding concern. Three-month bills yielded 9 basis points over SOFR OIS and six-month bills 13, which Barclays' Samuel Earl described as the highest relative levels this year and comparable with Q4 2025 money-market volatility. Continued bill cheapening could transmit into repo and ultimately the effective federal funds rate. The commentary raised possible reserve-management purchases after the Fed paused them last month; it did not report a new intervention.

## Forward Market Significance

September 30 combines the inflation and employment tests most relevant to Williams' proposed patience. ADP is due at 8:15 a.m. New York time, with September private employment expected to rise 70,000 after 38,000. At 8:30 a.m., August core PCE is expected up 0.3% monthly after 0.2%, with annual growth of 3.3%; headline prices are expected to rise 0.4% monthly. Spending is forecast to increase 0.8% and income 0.4%. The spending result will help determine whether weak confidence is beginning to restrain purchases, while inflation bears directly on how much time the Fed can allow after September's increase.

October 1 brings claims and ISM manufacturing, with the latter expected at 55 after 54.6 and its prices measure at 72.3 after 71.1. October 2 payrolls are expected to rise 90,000 after 162,000, with unemployment unchanged at 4.1% and monthly wage growth of 0.3%. Slower hiring without greater unemployment would extend Tuesday's low-hiring picture; deterioration beyond that could become particularly disruptive for the growing Treasury futures short positions. Further appearances by Barkin, Goolsbee, Kashkari and Williams will reveal whether the distinction between eventual tightening and immediate action spreads within the Fed.

Australia's monthly inflation release Wednesday follows a rate increase that markets interpreted more cautiously than the statement initially suggested. Euro-area inflation Friday, expected at 3.7%, follows Spain's upside surprise and the relief in European energy prices. Japan's Wednesday two-year auction will test policy-sensitive demand after strong reception at 40 years. These are different challenges: near-term inflation persistence, the breadth of Europe's price acceleration and investors' willingness to hold short Japanese duration.

Paramount's expected Wednesday pricing must convert revised order books into final funding costs. The shift toward loans has already improved that segment's terms, while reduced junk-bond demand leaves concessions consequential for the issuer's deleveraging arithmetic. France's Thursday budget presentation must establish whether the proposed spending effort can win parliamentary support alongside record planned issuance. For energy, the added U.S. reserve release provides actual supply relief, but unresolved Hormuz negotiations leave the persistence of high fuel costs central to both household demand and monetary policy.

In the separate early Asian session before 7:15 a.m. Taipei Wednesday, New Zealand bonds rallied after the mixed Treasury finish and WTI traded about 0.8% lower at $88.70. That opening extended the energy relief, while the completed U.S. session left a steeper curve and a still-rising cost of long-term borrowing.

section_summaries.summary: The market distinguished the timing of further Fed tightening from the cost of long-term capital. Williams eased the urgency of another increase, but weaker U.S. data and cheaper oil did not arrest the long-bond decline. Paramount adjusted its financing as demand diverged, high-yield spreads widened noticeably, and Australia's bond rally followed a softer message about the next hike rather than a reversal of tightening.

section_summaries.section_title: Williams Slows the Clock as the Treasury Curve Steepens
section_summaries.summary: Williams favored time to assess September's tightening, while other Fed officials remained concerned about persistent inflation. The 2s10s curve steepened 7.1 basis points as weaker openings and confidence supported the front end. Rising real yields and corporate supply weighed on longer debt even as oil and inflation compensation fell. Growing futures shorts could amplify an unwind on weak data, although positioning was not uniformly bearish.

section_summaries.section_title: Paramount Rebalances Its Financing as the Interest Bill Rises
section_summaries.summary: Paramount increased its dollar loan to $8.5 billion and cut planned higher-rated bonds to about $30 billion within a roughly $52 billion package. Loan margins improved as junk-bond orders shrank; a 10-year dollar note remained near a 9% yield. Its $6 billion savings plan implies 4.4 times leverage, versus rating agencies' roughly seven times after completion. Higher interest costs leave less cash for repayment and increase reliance on execution or asset sales.

section_summaries.section_title: Australia Hikes While Europe Gets Partial Energy Relief
section_summaries.summary: Australia raised rates to 4.6%, but three-year yields fell 8 basis points after Bullock expressed hope that enough tightening had been delivered. European bonds gained with cheaper energy despite Spain's inflation accelerating to 5%. Britain still paid its highest 10-year auction yield since 1999 as mortgage approvals weakened and consumer credit grew. Canada faced competing energy-inflation pressure and a new U.S. trade restriction.

section_summaries.section_title: Sovereigns Change the Amount and Maturity of New Debt
section_summaries.summary: New Zealand cut planned bond sales by NZ$15 billion over four years, while France set record 2027 issuance of €340 billion. Japan's 40-year auction drew strong demand after supply cuts. The Philippines chose a 2.5-year retail bond, and Thailand considered shorter funding to avoid locking in high rates. China's stimulus could raise local issuance; Bulgaria tightened euro-bond pricing, while Mexico's expanding pension base supported domestic funding.

section_summaries.section_title: Municipal Losses and AI Concentration Reach Investors
section_summaries.summary: Munis headed toward a 4.7% September loss amid heavy supply and record trade counts. Nuveen's roughly $190 million Brightline sale at 45 cents raised markdown risk even as restructuring support broadened. PGIM introduced a 15% AI-linked collateral limit in a $500 million Allstate CLO, capturing exposures across industries. Bain questioned the revenue needed to justify AI capital spending, while separate research cautioned against assuming a large fiscal dividend.

September 30 ADP and PCE, followed by claims, ISM and payrolls, test the case for Fed patience and the vulnerability of Treasury shorts. Paramount's expected Wednesday pricing will establish its funding costs. Australian and euro-area inflation, Japan's two-year auction and France's budget presentation pose distinct policy and financing tests, while unresolved Hormuz negotiations leave energy relief uncertain.

overall_summary.headline: Treasuries steepen as Williams signals patience but long-term borrowing costs keep rising
overall_summary.session_narrative:
John Williams said September's rate increase left the Fed time to gather information, with another move potentially appropriate late this year rather than urgently needed. October hike odds fell to about 50% from 70%. Job openings declined to 7.079 million and consumer confidence dropped to 81.9, reinforcing support for shorter maturities without ending the long-bond selloff.

The two-year yield fell 5.4 basis points to 4.878%, while the 30-year rose 3.7 to 5.585% after exceeding 5.61% during trading, its highest since 2002. At 10 years, real yields rose as inflation compensation declined: the pressure on long-term capital was not simply a rise in expected inflation. Paramount's large acquisition-financing launch added to supply pressure, and U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably.

Paramount shifted $2 billion of planned higher-rated bonds into its dollar loan as loan terms improved but junk-bond orders diminished. The eventual interest bill remains consequential for debt repayment. Overseas, Australia raised its cash rate to 4.6%, yet bonds rallied after Michele Bullock questioned the need for another increase. September 30 employment and inflation releases will test how much patience the Fed can afford.
